prompt: A national coffee chain is deciding whether to open cafés in airports. The candidate's framework: (1) Lease and operating costs at airports; (2) Rent and revenue-sharing terms with the airport; (3) Airport traveler demand and spending; (4) Competition from existing airport food outlets. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 1 and 2 overlap: both are what the airport charges
options.feedback: Right. Lease costs and rent or revenue-sharing terms are the same airport charges. Merge them and use the slot for whether the chain can run cafés inside airports.

options.text: Missing: whether the brand appeals to travelers
options.feedback: Brand appeal is part of traveler demand and spending, which bucket 3 covers. The real flaw is that buckets 1 and 2 both describe airport charges.

options.text: Bucket 4 doesn't belong: travelers have few other options at the gate
options.feedback: Few options is why the existing outlets matter: they decide how much of the traffic the chain can win.

options.text: It's a generic entry checklist: nothing in it is about airports
options.feedback: Every bucket is about airports: airport leases, traveler spending and airport outlets. The flaw is the overlap between buckets 1 and 2.

explanation: Buckets 1 and 2 both describe what the airport charges. A MECE version: traveler demand, competition, airport economics (lease, revenue share, staffing), and the chain's ability to operate in airports.

extras.corrected_framework: Traveler demand; competition; airport economics (lease, revenue share, staffing); ability to operate in airports
